propositions: Rebar's LLM runtime is Anthropic-shaped in practice with hardcoded provider checks scattered across runner.py, structured.py, and config.py that prevent first-class Bedrock support and reject base_url/api_key configuration despite documenting them

AWS Bedrock-hosted Claude cannot reach prompt caching, tenacity retries, per-request timeouts, or native structured output through an OpenAI-compatible gateway proxy, losing capabilities on the production path

The signed verdict sidecar records only a model string, not structured provider provenance (provider name, endpoint host, support tier, capabilities), making it impossible for consumers to distinguish first-class from best-effort sources

A provider_factory hook accepting a model string must return configured Provider objects with per-vendor ModelProfile overrides, replacing the inline anthropic branch and _NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS name-set matching

REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL and REBAR_LLM_API_KEY must compose with REBAR_LLM_MODEL_PROVIDER through a best-effort OpenAI-compatible builder without raising LLMConfigError, enabling local and third-party endpoints

Bedrock retry and timeout configuration is deferred — BedrockProvider currently receives only region_name with no botocore.config.Config, leaving llm_retry_max_attempts, llm_retry_max_wait_s, and timeout_s ineffective on the Bedrock path
